messages:

Cc: BigCo Legal <legal@bigco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@bigco.com>

Subject: Questions on termination windows for pilots and auto-renew

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. Before we finalize the order form we have a couple of questions from procurement/legal about Term/Renewal language:

- We saw the auto-renew language in the draft MSA and wanted to confirm whether pilot accounts (90-day free/discounted pilots) are eligible for the same renewal mechanics as paid deployments. Our preference is that pilots can be terminated for convenience with 30 days' notice rather than being locked into automatic renewals.
- Related: if Redwood insists on auto-renew across the board, could we ask for a staggered notice cadence (30 days for pilots, 60 days for paid deployments) to reduce inadvertent renewals?
- Are there commercial levers (e.g., a one-time onboarding fee or minimum invoice during the pilot) to offset the operational risk for Redwood if pilots can opt out sooner?

BigCo Legal also asked whether Redwood would accept language that preserves Redwood's right to charge a pro-rated minimum for customers who exit within X days of activation — they suggested an explicit minimum commitment for dedicated capacity.

We'd like to get this sorted before the countersign. Can you loop in whoever owns the MSA redlines?

Thanks,
Rachel

Subject: Re: Questions on termination windows for pilots and auto-renew

Hi Rachel — appreciate the clear questions.

Short answer: we're open to a staggered approach for pilots, but need legal sign-off on precise drafting and a commercial guardrail for short-duration exits. I've attached an initial redline to the MSA that proposes:

1) Pilot exception: "Pilot Accounts" (defined in the order form) may terminate for convenience with 30 days' prior written notice up to the end of the pilot term; such termination will not trigger auto-renewal.
2) Paid deployments: standard auto-renew remains, with a 60-day notice window to opt out prior to renewal.
3) Minimum liability/fee: for Dedicated or Reserved Capacity, we propose a 3-month pro-rated minimum if terminated within the first 90 days, to align onboarding costs.

Commercial note: If BigCo is fine with the staggered notice, Marissa and I can adjust the order form pricing to include the minimum for reserved capacity.

Looping in Aditya for legal / policy perspective and Marissa for commercial tradeoffs.

Best,
Kimberly

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on termination windows for pilots and auto-renew

Kim — quick legal perspective.

Thanks for the proposed redline. Legal is generally comfortable with the concept of a pilot carve-out, but asks that we:

- Narrow the definition of "Pilot Accounts" to avoid abuse (e.g., limit to non-production environments and a single pilot term per account).
- Keep auto-renew intact for any production or paid deployments that use dedicated capacity.
- Add an explicit sentence allowing Redwood to invoice a short-term commitment fee (we proposed a 3-month minimum for reserved capacity) and to withhold certain onboarding credits if the customer exits early.

One concern: if BigCo requests a blanket 30-day opt-out for any "pilot-like" usage, that could create churn and re-onboarding cost. If Marissa can propose how we would price that (or what minimum secures our onboarding), legal will sign off faster.

I recommend we offer (A) pilot exception with tight scope + (B) a 60-day renewal notice for paid usage + (C) a 90-day minimum billing for reserved capacity. That keeps commercial exposure constrained.

-Aditya

Team — commercial view: BigCo is strategic and likely to convert, but pilots are large (multi-seat, integrations) and have real setup costs. If we accept a 30-day pilot opt-out we should:

- Require the pilot to be scoped in an SOW with a clear acceptance milestone; if acceptance occurs we treat it as paid for purposes of notice windows.
- Apply a nominal onboarding fee of $5k for pilots that do not convert, or a 3-month minimum invoice for Reserved Capacity pilots.
- Add language that prevents consecutive "back-to-back" pilots for the same account without sales approval.

I need Laura's OK to approve commercial deviations from standard order form — looping her in for a one-off exception approval. If Laura signs off, I can present a counter that preserves renewal mechanics for paid usage while giving BigCo the pilot flexibility.

-Marissa

Subject: Re: Questions on termination windows for pilots and auto-renew — proposed path forward

Hi Rachel — thanks for the patience and the excellent questions. Summarizing the path we discussed internally and the edits we're prepared to propose: 

1) Pilot carve-out: we will add a narrowly defined "Pilot Account" concept (limited to non-production environments, single pilot term, SOW required). Pilots may terminate for convenience with 30 days' written notice prior to the pilot end date; such termination will prevent auto-renewal only for the pilot term.

2) Paid/Production deployments: standard auto-renew language remains. Customers must provide 60 days' prior written notice to opt out before a renewal period.

3) Commercial protection: for Reserved/Dedicated capacity, Redwood will implement a 90-day minimum billing period for accounts that activate reserved capacity; we will also include an optional onboarding fee (one-time) in the order form that can be used instead of the minimum.

4) Anti-abuse: pilots must be in a signed SOW with an acceptance milestone; consecutive pilots for the same account require written sales approval.

Next steps:
- Attached is the redline to the MSA (MSA_redline_kp_20261218.docx) and a proposed Order Form clause (OrderForm_Staggered_Notice_v1.pdf).
- If BigCo is comfortable, please confirm acceptance of the above items so we can circulate a countersigned MSA and update the order form.
- If Legal wants edits to the draft definition of "Pilot Account", please send a tracked change and we'll review promptly.

If helpful, Marissa is available for a short call tomorrow to align on the commercial offset.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
